scientific_question: When the evaluation horizon is sufficient to reach purchase, does hiding a retrieved action that is not admissible in the current state improve closed-loop WebShop behavior?
rationale: H1.20 changed navigation but all three arms produced zero buy actions under 15 steps. H1.21 matches the earlier 30-step carrier budget while preserving the same action-admissibility intervention.
hypothesis: At a 30-step horizon, TEXT-MEMORY-ADMISSIBLE-ONLY will selectively improve qualified-positive rate and/or paired task score over TEXT-MEMORY-RAW, while BASE remains the no-experience control.
controls: Only memory_action_policy changes between raw and admissible-only; admissible-only hides the recorded action only when its exact string is absent from the current Allowed actions list.

Model, tokenizer, prompt/action contracts, retrieval corpus, retrieval rule, optimizer state (none), temperature, max_new_tokens, environment seed, task panel, rollout seeds, GPU binding policy, and W&B online mode are frozen.
No teacher or oracle is used during evaluation; no evaluation result can enter the memory corpus.

metrics.primary: paired fresh-task qualified-positive rate and final task score: RAW versus ADMISSIBLE-ONLY
diagnostics: retrieval action admissibility and hidden-action count
parser/runtime failures outside the scientific denominator

stop_rule: If all arms have zero buy transitions or RAW versus FILTERED has zero paired gain, reconcile and stop this line; do not sweep horizon, rank, LR, epoch, or prompt.
positive_branch_rule: Only a selective filtered advantage across multiple partitions/tasks permits a fresh-task confirmation; it does not open Q3 by itself.
negative_branch_rule: Release GPUs, classify the bottleneck as broader base-agent/interface/task-family usability, and do not start another carrier micro-variant.
